human_gate.description: When a person is asked. in-the-loop, the default: at scope, every fold and the result. ends: at scope and the result. per-round: at every fold. exception: only for escalations.

not_findings.description: Path to the decided non-issues list

attack.description: How to attack in this lens: the techniques that find what the criteria call wrong

blocker.description: What blocks in this lens: its dimension's definition of a blocker, set when the repository is calibrated. Reviewers and the Judge get it, and a finding the Judge shows meets it blocks

include_generated.description: This lens's reviewers get generated files in the diff too

grayboard.description: With [grayboard] in config.toml: what a review waiting for you sends there, its questions in full (the default) or only that it waits.

generated.description: Generated files are left out of the diff a review sends, each listed with its line counts. Reviewers can still read them in the repository. Generated means by path: code generators' naming conventions, these paths, or the base's .gitattributes linguist-generated; never by a file's contents

exclude.description: Leave generated files out. Default true

paths.description: More paths that are generated, besides code generators' naming conventions

costs.description: What estimates are made from. A binding that sets its own prices in the user's config keeps them

prices.description: US dollars per million tokens, by model, or by binding name for a binding that names no model

cached_input_per_mtok.description: Input read from a cache. Left out, it costs what other input does

cache_write_per_mtok.description: Input written to a cache. Left out, it costs what other input does

per_call.description: Tokens each call by a role takes beyond the text ACR sends it and reads back: what its tools read, its turns, its thinking

stages.description: What every round does besides its lenses' reviewers. gate: first, before any reviewer, changed lines no test runs and breaks in changed code every test passes, told to every reviewer; with tests.gate: stop, a gap that blocks stops the round. brief: before the reviewers, the Orchestrator writes each lens a brief for this change: where to attack, and how. context: every role gets what the repository's history says about the changed files. claims: a lens that checks every claim the change makes about itself. mutation: a lens that proposes small breaks in the changed code, which the pipeline runs against the tests; a break they miss is a finding. probes: a lens that writes and runs scenarios of what the change says it does, which needs a binding with a shell. test-writing: between rounds of a review to convergence, a fresh writer pins each fixed blocker with a test that fails before the fix and passes after, and closes the gate's gaps. Left out, stages is [probes], or none when the reviewers' binding has no shell.

tests.description: How the repository's tests run, for the mutation stage.

command.description: Run from the repository's root. {tests} stands for the test files to run. Without it, it's found from the repository's files: Flutter, Cargo, Go, npm or pytest.

parallel.description: How many mutants run at once.

timeout.description: Seconds one run of the tests may take.

mutants.description: How many mutants a reviewer proposes in a round.

setup.description: Run once a round, from the root of a copy of the change, before any reviewer's copy is made from it: the package install and a first build, so every copy starts warm.

coverage.description: The command that runs the tests with coverage, from the root, writing an lcov report, for the gate.

report.description: Where the coverage report is, from the root: coverage/lcov.info if unset.

gate.description: What a gap that blocks does: warn and let the reviewers run (the default), or stop the round before them.

variants.description: Other ways the gate runs the change's own tests, each once, such as in random order, one at a time, or in another time zone.

command.description: From the root, with {tests} for the test files.

repeat.description: How many more times the gate runs the change's own tests plainly, after the first, to catch one that passes only sometimes.

runbook.description: How to work in this repository on this machine: setting up a copy, running its tests and probes, guarding a command that could hang, and where dependency and SDK sources are. Every role that can run things gets it.

allowed_models.description: The models a review of this repository may use, as patterns such as example/*, matched without regard to case. Every binding a review would call must name a model one of them matches, or the config is refused. Left out, any model the user's bindings name; set in the user's defaults, it holds every repository that doesn't set its own.

facts.description: How a round shares what tools found of the change (each changed file's definitions, where they're referenced, the tests that name them, and its hunks) and the test gate's results with its reviewers and Judges, ahead of their own text, so every call of a role reads them from the provider's prompt cache. Each field left out takes the default.

shared.description: Build the facts each round and give them to every reviewer and Judge. Default true.

warm_secs.description: Seconds the rest of a role's calls wait for its first to fill the prompt cache before they start. 0 starts them all at once. Default 60.

stagger_secs.description: Seconds between the starts of a role's other calls once its first has warmed the cache: a burst of new sessions can be spread over a provider's replicas, of which only one holds the prefix, where calls a little apart land on it. 0 starts them all at once. Default 3.

keep_alive_secs.description: Seconds between refreshes of a role's cached prefix while its calls run, so the provider doesn't evict it: a minimal call through the same binding, only when its bridge has a slot to spare, counted apart as keep-alive. 0 turns it off. Default 240.

judges.description: per-lens, the default: one Judge rates a lens's findings together. per-finding: a Judge for each finding, given its claim and the lines it cites, and none of the reviewer's reasoning.

reviewers.description: all, the default: reviewers get the Orchestrator's briefs and the decided non-issues too. facts-only: only what tools found, and no decided non-issues, which the Judge still applies.

match_tools.description: Give the reviewers and the Judge on one bridge and model the same tool definitions, the union of theirs, so their prompts share a cached prefix, and refuse a call to a tool outside a role's own. Only for an agent acrbus can hold to a list; others keep their own tools. Default true.

learned.description: Learn which files this repository's reviewers open, from their tool calls, and give the files they keep opening, whole, in later rounds' facts and the next review's, after the change's own, so a reviewer reads them from the prompt cache instead of spending turns to open them. Nothing a reviewer may open is taken away. Default true.

learned_bytes.description: The most bytes of such often-read files a round's facts carry. Every reviewer and Judge reads them again each turn, so they pay only when reviewers would open them early anyway: a file must have been opened by at least two reviewer calls, and one that doesn't fit is left out, which progress says. Default 24576.

savings.description: How a review saves on its Judges and later rounds, without taking anything a reviewer or Judge may read or use. Each field left out takes the default.

reuse_rulings.description: Carry a Judge's ruling over to a later round's finding that makes the same claim, in the same lens, at the same place in a file no fix has changed since, when that ruling didn't block. Anything else goes to a Judge. Default true.

first_pass_judge.description: A binding that rules on findings first, such as a cheaper model. What it would have block, rates Medium or above, calls a split or a values call, or marks unsure goes to the Judge's binding, which rules on it fresh, without the first pass's ruling. Left out, none. Check it with acr judge-check --first-pass before turning it on.

focus_after_fix.description: After a fix, tell each lens's reviewers what it changed and what it could affect (its references and tests) as where to look first. The whole change stays theirs. Default false.

blast_radius.description: After a fix, ask one small call on the Sizer's binding whether each lens that passed before the fix needs to attack again. A lens it skips is reported as skipped, with the reason, never as passing the new version. A lens with blockers of its own always attacks again. Default false.

group_fixes.description: Fix a round's blockers in groups, each in a fresh session on the Orchestrator's binding: blockers in the same files together, the rest each alone, one group after another in the checkout, each seeing what the groups before it changed. Default true.

fixer.description: A cheaper binding for the fix groups the rules call easy: every blocker in the group at or below max_severity, the group citing at most max_files files, each with its cause stated (file, line and detail), none a person's call or a defect a person reported missed, and none like one fixed in an earlier round. Every other group, and an easy group's restart after its fix failed, goes to the Orchestrator's binding, as do its other calls. Left out, the Orchestrator's binding fixes every group.

binding.description: A binding in allowed_bindings that may write.

max_severity.description: The most severe a blocker in an easy group may be. Default Medium.

max_files.description: The most files an easy group's blockers may cite. Default 1.

sessions.description: How long calls are broken into shorter sessions, each starting from the shared opening the prompt cache holds, instead of one session that rereads everything it has read on every turn, and when a call that logs no new turn is warned of. Relays and scouting are off unless set.

relay_tokens.description: By role, reviewer, judge or orchestrator: the prompt tokens of one turn past which a call hands off. It writes its findings so far, what it has checked and what's left, and a fresh session on the same binding carries on from there. An Orchestrator's relay is for its fixes: what it has fixed so far, and what's left. Only agents acrbus can steer mid-call (pi, through acrbus's extension) relay; others run whole.

stall_warn_secs.description: Seconds a call may log no new turn before progress warns of it, once, until it moves again. Nothing is cut off for it. 0 turns the warning off. Default 180.

scout.description: Lenses whose reviewers scout first: one session lists what it suspects, without verifying, then each suspicion is confirmed or dropped in a short session of its own, from the shared opening and that suspicion alone.
